NEW DELHI: The Congress spent a total Rs 248.6 crore on its campaign for the recent assembly elections in Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry, even as its total receipts between the date of announcement and completion of these polls stood at Rs 207.1 crore.According to Congress's election expenditure statement for the five state/UT polls, filed on July 31 with the Election Commission, the party received Rs 104 crore in cash and Rs 103.1 crore via cheque or draft between March 15, 2026, when the elections were announced, and May 6, 2026, when they had concluded.The Congress's full poll expense statement shows its total opening balance of cash in hand (including at the level of its central headquarters and the state/district/local level units of the 5 states/UTs) at Rs 22.9 crore and its cash in bank at Rs 146.1 crore. At the end of the polls, its cash in hand was marginally lower at Rs 22.6 crore while its bank balance had declined by 45% to Rs 80.6 crore.On the expenditure side, the party declared a total spend of Rs 143 crore on general party propaganda and Rs 105.6 crore on candidates. The latter includes Rs 95.5 crore given by the party as lump-sum payments to its candidates across the five poll-gone states/UT; while the central party headquarters bore Rs 95.3 crore of expenditure under this head, the state/district/local units disbursed only Rs 23 lakh among the candidates.Expenses on virtual campaigns through social media platforms and applications were declared at Rs 6.8 crore.Over Rs 3.2 crore was spent by the Congress on publicising the criminal antecedents of its candidates.As part of general party propaganda, the Congress spent Rs 92.5 crore on media advertisements, covering print and electronic space, bulk SMS, cable TV, websites and TV channels. Another Rs 8 crore funded public meetings, processions and rallies, while Rs 11.5 crore was spent on badges, posters, cutouts, hoardings etc and nearly Rs 2 crore on miscellaneous propaganda items.Poll surveys and campaigns for the five assembly elections cost the Congress Rs 4.8 crore.A total Rs 23.5 crore was spent by the grand old party on the travel and lodging of its star campaigners (Rs 21.8 crore) and other leaders. The aircraft and helicopters were sourced from Air Charter Services Pvt Ltd, Aircab Aviation, A R Airways, GMP Air Charter, Lima Tang Aviation Service, Devigo Data Systems and Global Vectra.The Congress's central headquarters routed Rs 83.2 crore of its lump-sum payments to candidates through the state/UT units; with Kerala unit getting the largest share at Rs 55.1 crore, followed by Puducherry (Rs 10 crore), West Bengal (Rs 9 crore), Tamil Nadu (Rs 7.1 crore) and Assam (Rs 2 crore).The Congress-led UDF seized power in Kerala, but the party or its alliances performed poorly in other states, managing 21 seats in Assam, 6 in Puducherry and 2 in West Bengal, while drawing a blank in Tamil Nadu.

Article Title: ‘MPs should not be reduced’: Udhayanidhi Stalin backs TVK's resolution against delimitation

NEW DELHI: DMK on Wednesday supported the Tamil Nadu government’s resolution opposing the Centre’s proposed delimitation exercise, with Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin saying the state’s representation in the Lok Sabha should not be reduced.He said the number of Members of Parliament from Tamil Nadu should not be reduced in the name of delimitation and called for the exercise to be deferred for 25 years."In the name of constituency delimitation, the number of Members of Parliament should not be reduced. Our stand is that constituency delimitation should not be carried out for the next 25 years. We welcome the resolution on the 33% reservation for women. Our firm stand is that Tamil Nadu should not be affected by constituency delimitation. The movement that first told India what the impact of delimitation would be is the DMK," Udhayanidhi added.The development comes after Tamil Nadu assembly on Wednesday passed a resolution in the state Assembly opposing the Union government’s proposed delimitation exercise.Speaking in the assembly, CM Vijay also called for the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections based on the existing 543 constituencies."The 33% reservation for women should be implemented in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections itself, based on the existing 543 constituencies. The 33% reservation for women should not be delayed any further. In Tamil Nadu, more women have voted than men. Providing reservation for women is not a concession; it is a matter of social justice. The 33% reservation for women must be implemented without any further delay," he said.The resolution seeks to safeguard the political representation of southern states, particularly Tamil Nadu, arguing that their success in controlling population growth should not result in reduced representation in Parliament."All the states including Tamil Nadu and the people / elected representatives of the union territories have not had their population counted for more than 50 years. The next census to count the population was supposed to be held in 2026. Therefore, since the delimitation of constituencies has not been carried out for the last 50 years, based on the 2011 population census, the constituencies should be delimited and the number of Lok Sabha and Assembly members should be increased from 550 to 850 by bringing in a constitutional amendment Bill," the resolution stated.The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, was introduced in the Lok Sabha on April 16, proposing to increase the strength of the Lower House to 850 seats and expedite the implementation of the Women's Reservation Bill passed in 2023. However, the Bill failed to secure the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of members present and voting and was not passed.While the Congress and other opposition parties have supported the Women's Reservation Bill, they have opposed the proposed delimitation exercise and called for an increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats. The Opposition has also demanded that women's reservation be delinked from delimitation.
Article Summary: DMK supports Tamil Nadu government's resolution opposing Centre's proposed delimitation exercise. Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin says state's representation in Lok Sabha should not be reduced. NEW DELHI: A key objective of the govt under the Nuclear Energy Mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033, minister for department of atomic energy Jitendra Singh said in a written reply in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is undertaking the design and development of indigenous SMR technologies, including the 220 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor (BSMR-200) and 55 MWe SMR-55 for power generation. BARC is also developing a high temperature gas cooled reactor (HTGCR) of up to 5 MW capacity, which can be coupled with a suitable thermochemical cycle for hydrogen production.Singh said India is steadily strengthening its indigenous nuclear energy ecosystem with a focus on advanced reactor technologies, SMRs, domestic manufacturing capabilities, private-sector participation and long-term utilisation of the country’s abundant thorium resources. The govt has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition. This includes deployment of large indigenous reactors such as 700 MWe pressurised heavy water reactors (PHWRs) and advanced reactor designs at greenfield sites, alongside development and deployment of SMRs at brownfield locations, including retiring fossil-fuel-based power plants, captive plants for energy-intensive industries and off-grid applications in remote areas.The minister also highlighted continuing work of the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) in advancing the second stage of India’s nuclear power programme. IGCAR is pursuing multidisciplinary scientific research and advanced engineering development for sodium cooled fast breeder reactors and associated closed fuel-cycle facilities, technologies that remain a cornerstone of India’s long-term nuclear strategy.On thorium, Singh said India is pursuing its three-stage nuclear power programme, based on a closed fuel cycle, to optimise utilisation of its uranium resources and progressively harness its abundant thorium reserves. Thorium, being a fertile material, needs to be converted into fissile uranium-233 in a nuclear reactor before it can be used for energy generation.India has already undertaken sustained R&D towards thorium utilisation. Thorium Oxide (Thoria) pellets have been used in the initial cores of operating PHWRs, while Thoria-based fuels have also been irradiated in BARC research reactors. The irradiated Thoria pins have been reprocessed to obtain uranium-233, which has subsequently been fabricated as fuel for the KAMINI reactor at IGCAR, Kalpakkam. Singh said the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, 2025 has been enacted to enable wider participation of both public and private entities in the nuclear sector.
Article Summary: The govt under the Nuclear Energy Mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033. Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is undertaking the design and development of indigenous SMR technologies. The govt has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition.

Article Title: Supreme Court pushes 19 states, union territories to notify cancer
Article Text:
Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting

NEW DELHI: With the National Cancer Registry Programme covering only a fraction of India’s population and rural cancer surveillance remaining particularly limited, the Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting. The court on Tuesday asked the 19 States and Union Territories that have not yet notified cancer as a notifiable disease to consider doing so, a move that could make reporting of newly detected cases to public health authorities mandatory.Such notification could help plug gaps in cancer surveillance by giving health authorities a more complete picture of the country’s cancer burden, including where cases are rising and which populations are most affected. The data could in turn help shape policies on prevention, early detection, treatment capacity and allocation of healthcare resources.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant passed the order on a plea filed by a retired AIIMS doctor after his lawyer Gaurav Bansal told the court that NCRP covers only 10% of population and rural coverage is less than 1%.The push assumes greater significance against the backdrop of the WHO’s latest Global Status Report on Cancer, which estimates that 92% of people globally will be affected by cancer either directly or through a close family member.The report also projects annual cancer cases to rise to nearly 35 million by 2050.The Supreme Court was informed that 17 of India’s 36 States and UTs have already notified cancer, following recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare. The remaining 19 have now been asked to consider similar action.Dr Pragya Shukla, Head of Clinical Oncology at Delhi State Cancer Institute, said standardised, disease-specific and timely data was essential to track India's changing cancer burden, identify regional and demographic trends, and assess the impact of prevention and treatment programmes. Such a system, she said, would complement existing cancer registries, help identify high-burden areas, improve planning for treatment infrastructure and medicines, and strengthen evidence-based cancer control. Govil added that reliable data would be critical for planning prevention, early detection and resource allocation.The Indian Cancer Society welcomed the intervention, saying national notification could help build a comprehensive cancer surveillance system. “The Supreme Court’s intervention is a significant development, and we welcome its direction to the remaining States and Union Territories to move towards cancer notification,” said Jyotsna Govil, Chairperson, Indian Cancer Society, Delhi. However, she stressed that notification alone would not suffice and called for a uniform national framework with common definitions, reporting standards and data protocols to ensure comparable and interoperable data across states.
Article Summary: Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting. The court on Tuesday asked the 19 States and Union Territories that have not yet notified cancer as a notifiable disease to consider doing so. The move could make reporting of newly detected cases to public health authorities mandatory.

Article Title: “It’s frustrating to still not see healthier options for kids”: How Savannah James’ $40 million philanthropic legacy with LeBron James is making a difference beyond basketball

Her business moves show why Savannah James has built an identity of her own

Savannah James has built a public identity that goes well beyond being LeBron James ’ wife. Her work in business and philanthropy has given her a platform of her own, with children and education often at the center of her efforts.One of the clearest examples came in 2018, when she joined K+ Organics as a founding partner. The company focused on creating healthier sports drinks for young athletes. At the same time, Savannah also played a visible role in the charitable work connected to the James family, including education initiatives that have committed more than $40 million.Savannah James did not enter the children's beverage business simply because it fit her family's celebrity profile. Her motivation came from a problem she noticed while raising three children who played sports.In May 2018, Forbes reported that Savannah had partnered with Velana Colón as an investor and co-owner of K+ Organics. The company aimed to offer a sports drink designed specifically for children rather than adapting products created for adult athletes.Savannah explained her thinking to Forbes in 2018, saying, “In this day and age, there are so many more healthy alternatives for adults than we had...growing up, but it’s frustrating to still not see healthier options for kids.”Those remarks capture why the venture is important to her. Savannah was looking at the market from a parent's perspective. She wanted an option that made more sense for young athletes and families.The partnership also gave her a chance to put that belief into a product. In March 2018, K+ Organics announced a new Lemonade flavor developed with Savannah. The company said the 16.9-ounce drink contained 80 calories and included vitamins B5, B6 and B12.Savannah's business work represents one side of her influence. Her connection to LeBron James' philanthropic efforts shows another.The James family's education work in Akron grew significantly through the I Promise initiative. The LeBron James Family Foundation partnered with the University of Akron in August 2015 to provide eligible students with a pathway toward a four-year college scholarship. The initiative later became closely associated with the James family's broader commitment to education.The SportsRush previously reported that the foundation had pledged nearly $40 million toward scholarships for underprivileged students. Various reports has also described the LeBron James Family Foundation as having committed more than $40 million toward education initiatives.Savannah's role matters because her philanthropy has never stopped at one project. In 2016, she helped Akron high school seniors with prom dresses through her I PROMise Makeover initiative. She also founded Women of Our Future, a mentorship program aimed at supporting high school girls in Akron.That makes the $40 million figure part of a much bigger family effort rather than a standalone donation by Savannah herself.Savannah's entrepreneurial path started before K+ Organics. In December 2013, she opened The Juice Spot, a cold-pressed juice bar in Miami's Brickell neighborhood. She developed the concept with her trainer, David Alexander, and focused the menu on juices, smoothies and light bites.The Juice Spot eventually closed after the James family moved back to Cleveland. Eater Miami reported in January 2016 that Savannah struggled to manage the Miami location from afar after LeBron returned to Cleveland.She also entered the furniture business, working with American Signature on the Home Court collection. Her ventures show a consistent pattern: Savannah James has used her interests in family, health, design and education to build projects that extend beyond basketball.LeBron James may remain the biggest name in the family, but Savannah's work has created a lane of her own. From healthier choices for young athletes to education and mentorship in Akron, her impact reaches well beyond the court.

Article Title: Meet Connor Hill, the 17-year-old Pennsylvania student who wrote a computer program to classify noble polyhedra; he proved there are 146 isolated examples and won $250,000
Article Text:
Connor Hill (Delta High School, State College, PA)

Solving a long-standing geometry problem

Connecting pure mathematics with other areas of science

Explaining how he solved the problem, Hill said:

He also explained why mathematics is useful for solving difficult scientific problems:

National awards and support for young researchers

By writing a custom computer algorithm that mapped every possible version of a rare class of geometric shapes, 17-year-old Connor Hill from Port Matilda, Pennsylvania, has won the top $250,000 prize at the 2026 Regeneron Science Talent Search.His computational proof classified a complex group of three-dimensional shapes called noble polyhedra. His work identified two infinite structural families and exactly 146 separate, isolated examples.The announcement was made jointly by Regeneron Pharmaceuticals and Society for Science at a black-tie ceremony at the National Building Museum in Washington, D.C. The competition, now in its 85th year, is widely recognised as the oldest and one of the most prestigious science and mathematics competitions for high school seniors in the United States.Polyhedra are three-dimensional shapes made from flat polygonal faces and straight edges. Common examples include cubes, pyramids and octahedrons.A polyhedron is called noble when it has a high level of symmetry. Every face must have the same shape, and every vertex, or corner, must have the same arrangement of faces. A cube is a simple example because all six faces are squares and all eight corners have the same structure.Noble polyhedra, however, allow more complicated and even self-intersecting shapes than the familiar Platonic solids. This makes their classification a much harder mathematical problem.Before Hill's research, mathematicians had already identified two infinite families of noble polyhedra. However, the complete list of individual, isolated shapes was still unknown.By 2020, researchers had confirmed 61 isolated examples, but they believed that many more could exist because of more complicated combinations of symmetry.To solve the problem, Hill created a custom computer program that could systematically examine all possible geometric arrangements. Instead of trying to search through an endless number of three-dimensional shapes directly, he converted the problem into algebraic equations, including polynomial equations. This allowed the computer to reduce the problem to a finite set of possibilities that could be checked.According to research summaries released in the Society for Science 2026 Regeneron STS media kit, Hill's program completed the exhaustive search and showed that there are exactly 146 isolated noble polyhedra, in addition to the two known infinite families.Hill's work was not only about finding the number of noble polyhedra. He also believes that the method he developed could be useful in other areas of science and mathematics.In a discussion published on Regeneron's scientific portal after the award announcement, Hill spoke about his approach with Dr. Henry Wei, Executive Director of Development Innovation at Regeneron."By translating the problem into a different mathematical framework, I could narrow it down to a finite set that could actually be solved."Hill said his interest in the problem began through his involvement in an online geometry community, where the classification of noble polyhedra had been discussed as an open mathematical challenge."Science gives us the concepts, but math allows us to formalize them and apply them. When we're solving big problems, the key is breaking them into smaller pieces that math can address. Often, breakthroughs happen when someone connects ideas across disciplines."Dr. Wei pointed out that Hill's approach of turning a complicated problem into smaller, solvable parts is similar to methods used in modern biomedical research. Scientists use mathematical models to study problems such as protein folding, disease development and how drugs interact with the body.Hill hopes his computational method can eventually be used to study compound polyhedral structures and connected geometric networks.The 2026 Regeneron Science Talent Search awarded more than $1.8 million to 40 high school finalists. The finalists were selected from thousands of students who applied from across the United States.Second place and a $175,000 prize went to 17-year-old Edward Kang of Hackensack, New Jersey. Kang developed an artificial intelligence screening tool called RetinaMind.Kang trained machine-learning models using retinal scans to identify subtle blood-vessel patterns associated with autism and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. He also created cellular models to study related genetic changes.Third place and a $150,000 prize went to 17-year-old Iris Shen of The Woodlands, Texas. Shen studied possible treatments for blood cancer using clams as a testing model. She observed cellular responses that were similar to those seen in human drug trials.Maya Ajmera, President and CEO of Society for Science and Executive Publisher of Science News, praised the finalists in an official statement released by Society for Science."Congratulations to the winners of this year's Regeneron Science Talent Search," Ajmera said. "Their bold vision and perseverance reveal what the next generation of problem solvers truly looks like—and why our future is in capable hands. Their creativity, ambition and courage to confront the world's toughest challenges are exactly what this moment demands."Regeneron also highlighted the importance of supporting young researchers. Dr. George D. Yancopoulos, co-founder, Board Co-Chairman, President and Chief Scientific Officer of Regeneron, is himself a 1976 winner of the competition."Congratulations to the winners of the 2026 Regeneron Science Talent Search, and to all the finalists who participated in this year's competition," Yancopoulos said. "These students represent exactly the kind of extraordinary talent scientific progress depends on."Alongside the 2026 awards, Regeneron announced a 10-year extension of its title sponsorship of the competition through 2036. The company pledged another $150 million to support STEM education programs and scientific competitions run by Society for Science.Hill plans to attend the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in the autumn, where he will continue studying computational mathematics.
Article Summary: 17-year-old Connor Hill from Port Matilda, Pennsylvania, has won the top $250,000 prize at the 2026 Regeneron Science Talent Search. His computational proof classified a complex group of three-dimensional shapes called noble polyhedra. His work identified two infinite structural families and exactly 146 separate, isolated examples.

Article Title: In 2020, Minnesota funded a $1.918 million Shell Rock River habitat program; by 2025, it had protected or restored 588 acres
Article Text:
Shell Rock River Watershed District (Image Credit: www.shellrock.org)

A habitat program takes shape

Three properties protected

Wetlands and prairie restored

More acres than planned

A longer-term conservation effort

In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. According to a 2025 final report from the Lessard-Sams Outdoor Heritage Council, the program ultimately protected, restored or enhanced 588 acres of habitat in the Shell Rock River watershed, exceeding its original goal of 483 acres.The funding was provided under Minnesota Laws 2020, with the appropriation directed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources for an agreement with the Shell Rock River Watershed District. The funding was intended to support land acquisition as well as the restoration and enhancement of aquatic habitat within the watershed. The program focused on several types of conservation work, including acquiring properties, restoring wetlands and improving aquatic habitat. The projects were selected using conservation planning and monitoring intended to identify areas where habitat improvements could provide significant benefits.The Shell Rock River Watershed is a shallow-lake system that supports fish, waterfowl and other wildlife. According to the final report, restoration projects were targeted at addressing habitat degradation and improving conditions for native fish, waterfowl and wildlife.One part of Phase IX involved acquiring three properties: the Glenville Property, the Bancroft Property, and the Church Lake Property. The District closed on the Glenville Property in March 2021 and the Bancroft Property in September 2021. For the Church Lake Property, the District transferred the deed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources in December 2024 after acquiring and restoring the parcel.The final report says these acquisitions contributed to the program's permanent protection of 218 acres. Another 370 acres of habitat and wetlands were enhanced or restored through the program. Together, those accomplishments contributed to the reported total of 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored.The program included several restoration projects beyond property acquisition. The Bancroft Wetland Restoration was initiated in 2020, with construction beginning in June 2024 and largely completed by the fall of that year. Additional seeding work was completed in spring 2025. Another project focused on Panicum Prairie, where habitat enhancement work was carried out across 300 acres. The project involved native prairie vegetation and was substantially completed in February 2025, with final work completed in May.The program also supported the Fountain Lake In-Lake Habitat Project. Work included additional rock reefs and rock boulder clusters intended to improve fish habitat. The report notes that Phase IX funds were used to expand the scope of this work after the District determined additional funds were available. These projects addressed different parts of the watershed's ecosystem, from wetlands and prairie habitat to aquatic areas. The broader aim was to improve habitat conditions while protecting areas that could provide long-term benefits for wildlife.The program's original accomplishment plan called for 483 acres. By the end of the project, the final total had reached 588 acres, 105 acres more than initially planned. The report attributes the increase to the addition of the In-Lake Habitat Project and the Church Lake Property to Phase IX.According to the report, all grant funds were spent. The final grant expenditure remained $1.918 million, while the program's final total including leverage was $1.9479 million.The work is intended to continue beyond the end of the grant. The Shell Rock River Watershed District relies on multiple funding sources, including a local option sales tax, local levy and public funding, to maintain conservation projects. The Minnesota Department of Natural Resources will also maintain the Church Lake Property, which it owns.The program's results illustrate how a single state-funded conservation effort can combine land protection, wetland restoration, prairie enhancement and aquatic habitat improvements. Rather than focusing on one habitat type, Phase IX combined several projects across the Shell Rock River watershed. By 2025, the program had moved beyond its original target, with the final report recording 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored. The completed work represents a combination of permanent land protection and habitat improvements designed to support Minnesota's fish, waterfowl and wildlife over the long term.
Article Summary: In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. By 2025, the program had moved beyond its original target, with the final report recording 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored.

Article Title: Upset Paramount may leave California; company says it has duty towards shareholders, and that ultimately, you go to the place where you ...
Article Text:
Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. merger under fire

Jobs and economy

Paramount Skydance reported mixed earnings results

Paramount Skydance’s chief legal officer Makan Delrahim has suggested that the company could leave California as it faces mounting antitrust scrutiny from the state government. According to a report by The Hill, speaking at Politico’s The The California Agenda: Sacramento Summit, Delrahim said CEO David Ellison remains committed to California but emphasized there is a point where the company has a fiduciary duty to shareholders. “You have to take a look at the business environment and look to see what’s best for not only the community and the business. And ultimately, you know, go to the place where you’re wanted,” he said.Paramount, based in Los Angeles, agreed last month to pause its multibillion-dollar acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery after litigation was filed by California’s attorney general and 11 other states. The lawsuit argues the deal would give Paramount excessive power in news, entertainment, and sports media, harming competition. A trial is scheduled for next spring.The merger has drawn criticism from Democrats and media watchdogs, who worry that Warner Bros.Discovery’s CNN could fall under the influence of Ellison, an ally of President Trump and son of Oracle founder Larry Ellison. Ellison defended the deal in a New York Times op-ed, writing: “I do not aspire to lead these companies to bend their newsrooms to my views.”Delrahim argued the lawsuit is harming employment, saying: “This merger is actually going to be good — not only for California — it’ll be good for America.” Paramount maintains that its duty to shareholders may ultimately force it to relocate if California continues to oppose the merger.Recently, Paramount Skydance reported mixed second-quarter results, with revenue rising 1% year-over-year to $6.91 billion, beating estimates, while profit fell short at $41 million. Streaming revenue grew 9% to nearly $2.5 billion, driven by subscriber gains from Paramount+ content including UFC Freedom 250 and the FIFA World Cup. Studio revenue reached $1.3 billion, though theatrical performance lagged compared to last year’s Mission: Impossible — The Final Reckoning.
Article Summary: Paramount Skydance’s chief legal officer Makan Delrahim has suggested that the company could leave California as it faces mounting antitrust scrutiny. Delrahim said CEO David Ellison remains committed to California but emphasized there is a point where the company has a fiduciary duty to shareholders.

Article Title: Phoebe Gates’ shopping app Phia responds to 'cookie stuffing' allegations, says have started issuing ...
Article Text:
Phoebe Gates' Phia responds to cookie stuffing allegations

What Phia spokesperson said

What is cookie stuffing that Phoebe Gates’ Phia is accused of

Phia, the AI-powered shopping startup founded by Bill Gates daughter Phoebe Gates and her Stanford roommate Sophia Kianni said that it is reviewing every transaction carefully and will reverse sales that were incorrectly attributed to it, says a report by People. The development comes days after a Bloomberg report said that the two founders were aware of ‘cookie stuffing’ – a practice where affiliate tracking cookies are placed on a user's browser without their knowledge, allowing a company to claim commission on purchases even when it did not influence the sale. The report cites internal Slack messages, people familiar with the matter and historical source code saying that both Gates and Kianni were aware of automatic cookie-setting features months earlier.The People report quotes a Phia spokesperson who told the publication:“Any features causing misattributions were immediately removed over a month ago on July 7. We are reviewing every transaction, we are fully committed to and have already begun issuing all transaction reversals to brand partners as a result of any misattribution, and we are hiring a head of compliance to make sure something like this never happens again.”“We are now continuing to connect our users with items and offers from thousands of brand partners,” the spokesperson continued, further adding “We will learn from this and want to ensure our users have the best possible shopping experience, with features like our new digital closet and more to come.”The statement did not address Bloomberg’s latest accusationsPhia operates as a browser extension designed to help shoppers automatically find discount codes and compare prices at online checkout counters. In exchange, partner retailers pay the platform an affiliate commission when its software helps convert a sale.However, internal chats accessed by the publication reveal that Phia implemented automated features that injected its tracking cookies into a shopper’s checkout session without requiring any user interaction, such as clicking a deal link or applying a coupon code, the Bloomberg report said. By dropping tracking identifiers automatically, Phia claimed credit and commissions for transactions it did not drive, a practice widely known as cookie stuffing and that is strictly prohibited by commercial network contracts and partner agreements.
Article Summary: Phia, the AI-powered shopping startup founded by Bill Gates daughter Phoebe Gates and her Stanford roommate Sophia Kianni said that it is reviewing every transaction carefully and will reverse sales that were incorrectly attributed to it. The development comes days after a Bloomberg report said that the two founders were aware of ‘cookie stuffing’ – a practice where affiliate tracking cookies are placed on a user's browser without their knowledge.

Article Title: China takes aim at Elon Musk’s ‘Jesus-level’ brain-chip dream with first BCI surgery policy
Article Text:
Repesentative image

A first-of-its-kind insurance policy

How the technology works

The 'Jesus-level technology'

Clinical trials in China and safety concerns

Government push

Elon Musk has spent years pursuing what he has called "Jesus-level" technology through Neuralink, aiming to treat chronic health conditions by implanting computer chips directly into the human brain. But that vision may end up taking shape fastest not in the US, but in China, where state authorities have launched a coordinated push to accelerate the country's own brain-computer interface (BCI) industry, according to a South China Morning Post report. China has introduced its first commercial policy covering invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) surgery. State-owned PICC Property and Casualty announced the scheme in partnership with a hospital affiliated with Zhejiang University School of Medicine in Hangzhou, a tech hub home to leading AI and robotics start-ups.Over the past few days, a string of BCI-related initiatives have been announced across China, involving state insurers, investment banks and local governments alike. The most significant came on Wednesday, when PICC Property and Casualty, a major state-owned insurer, announced it had signed the country's first commercial insurance policy covering the invasive surgery typically required to implant a BCI device in a patient's brain.The announcement moved markets almost immediately, with BCI-linked stocks in Hong Kong climbing as investors bet that insurance coverage would help speed up the technology's path to commercial use. Shares of BCI-related firms rose 1.59% on Wednesday, with neuro-interventional device maker Shanghai Heartcare Medical Technology up 1.28% and software developer BrainAurora Medical Technology gaining 1.65%.The BCI technology, which conventionally involves open-skull surgery to implant electrodes in a targeted region of the brain, allows patients to control digital devices using thought alone. The field has been most prominently championed globally by Musk's Neuralink, and versions of the technology have already been tested on human patients in both the US and China, in some cases showing promise in helping patients paralysed from the neck down regain the ability to move.The public hospital involved in PICC's new insurance scheme is regarded by local officials and doctors as a leading centre for BCI clinical trials in the region, and has reportedly conducted at least 12 human trials involving BCI implants, according to Chinese media reports. In one recent case, a 61-year-old paraplegic patient with a spinal cord injury regained the ability to bend and lift his leg within three days of surgery, and was walking unassisted by the fifteenth day.Brain-computer interfaces allow signals generated by the brain to be converted into digital commands that can control computers, devices or prosthetics. Musk has repeatedly promoted the technology's potential to transform lives. Speaking via video link at an event in Israel this week, Musk argued that his company, Neuralink, does not receive enough recognition for its achievements."Restoring control of people who are tetraplegics and restoring sight, I think, are pretty big deals," Musk said. "They're sort of what I might call Jesus-level technologies," he added. Neuralink has said its implants could eventually allow users to type, move a computer cursor and operate devices using only their thoughts. Supporters of the technology envision an even more ambitious future, where people could communicate digitally through thoughts or interact with machines without physical input.BCI technology, championed by Elon Musk’s Neuralink, requires open-skull surgery to implant electrodes that allow patients to control digital devices with their thoughts. In Hangzhou, doctors have conducted at least 12 human trials. In one case, a 61-year-old paraplegic regained the ability to walk unassisted within 15 days of surgery.Clinicians cautioned that safety must remain the top priority. “We don’t yet have long-term safety data from BCI clinical trials. There’s no data spanning several years,” said Duan Wanru, chief physician at Xuanwu Hospital in Beijing, during the Global Health Summit in Hong Kong.Alongside the insurance policy, the Zhejiang provincial government announced plans to boost financing for BCI firms and encourage them to go public. The coordinated effort underscores China’s ambition to lead in brain-computer interface technology, potentially outpacing Musk’s vision of “Jesus-level” implants to treat chronic conditions.
Article Summary: China has introduced its first commercial policy covering invasive brain- computer interface (BCI) surgery. BCI technology, championed by Elon Musk’s Neuralink, requires open-skull surgery to implant electrodes that allow patients to control digital devices with their thoughts. In Hangzhou, doctors have conducted at least 12 human trials.

Article Title: America’s biggest investor Michael Burry, who warned Wall Street of 2008 housing crisis, is not happy with Oracle and Micron, here's why
Article Text:
Michael Burry’s concerns about Oracle

The AI hype problem of Micron

Michael Burry is not happy with reports of Nvidia investing $250 billion in OpenAI

America’s biggest investor Michael Burry who famous for warning about the 2008 housing crisis has taken aim at two major technology players Oracle and Micron Technology. According to a report by The Street, known for his contrarian bets, Burry argues that both companies are overexposed to the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom and weighed down by financial commitments that could backfire if demand slows.As per the report, Burry disclosed a short position against Oracle, highlighting its massive spending on AI infrastructure. The company has signed long-term leases and GPU capacity contracts worth hundreds of billions, far exceeding its current revenue base. Despite the strong operating cash flow, Oracle reported negative free cash flow due to surging capital expenditures. Burry warns that if AI demand falters, Oracle could be left with costly obligations and declining returns.Micron Technology is also in Burry’s crosshairs. He expanded his short bet against the chipmaker, arguing its recent rally is driven more by investor enthusiasm for AI than by solid fundamentals. Micron has historically struggled with cyclical downturns, and Burry believes its profitability remains vulnerable despite the current boom.Burry’s bearish stance extends beyond individual companies. He has also shorted the iShares Semiconductor ETF and Nebius Group, signaling broader doubts about the sustainability of AI-linked stocks.His thesis centers on off-balance-sheet liabilities: companies committing billions to long-term infrastructure at inflated prices, which could become burdensome if growth slows.Recently, Michael Burry voiced his sharp criticism of reports that Nvidia is preparing a a $250 billion backstop for OpenAI’s massive Ohio data-center project. According to a report by the Wall Street journal, the guarantees would help OpenAI lease a 10-gigawatt site being developed by SoftBank’s SB Energy, with total costs potentially exceeding $500 billion. Burry’s complaint echoes what analysts have long warned about in AI megadeals: circular funding arrangements that expose investors to enormous risk if sentiment shifts or growth slows. Nvidia, already valued at $5 trillion, has invested $30 billion in OpenAI and is now considering financing chip purchases worth another $350 billion. Critics say such structures could leave the industry vulnerable, especially since OpenAI remains unprofitable and lacks an investment-grade credit rating.Michael Burry’s criticism underscores growing unease about the sustainability of $100 billion-plus AI financing structures. His warning suggests that while AI demand is surging, the industry’s reliance on complex guarantees and debt-backed megaprojects could become its biggest vulnerability.
Article Summary: America's biggest investor Michael Burry has taken aim at two major technology players Oracle and Micron Technology. Burry argues that both companies are overexposed to the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom and weighed down by financial commitments that could backfire if demand slows.

Article Title: Oracle layoffs: As Oracle leadership prepares to send ‘6am layoff email’ on September 1, company asks managers to give a list of…
Article Text:
Oracle cut 21,000 jobs last year. Another round is coming this month

Oracle layoffs in March arrived as 6AM emails for 10,000+ employees and ended the same working day

Oracle has burned through almost all of its $2.1 billion restructuring budget

Why Oracle's $55.7 billion AI data centre spending keeps the pressure on headcount

Oracle is lining up another round of job cuts this month, and the deadline is set by its own calendar. Managers have been asked to draw up lists of employees whose roles are being eliminated, with the company looking to bring payroll down before September 1—the day its fiscal second quarter opens. Business Insider, which first reported the plan citing people familiar with it and an internal document, said reductions on some teams could reach double-digit percentages.The cuts would land on top of a year in which the company already removed about 21,000 full-time roles, roughly 13% of its workforce. Headcount fell from around 162,000 in May 2025 to about 141,000 at the end of May 2026, with roughly 49,000 of those remaining in the United States. What makes this round sting is Oracle's own explanation. Its annual filing attributes part of the decline to the company's adoption and deployment of AI—the same technology it is borrowing tens of billions of dollars to sell.Employees cut on March 31 found out first thing in the morning. The notification, sent from "Oracle Leadership," told recipients their role had been eliminated as part of a broader organisational change and that it was their last working day.Staff in both the US and India were affected. LinkedIn posts from those let go pointed to Oracle Health, Sales, Cloud, Customer Success and NetSuite. Roughly 10,000 positions went in that single wave.The email itself was brisk. It thanked employees for their contributions, told them severance paperwork would arrive via DocuSign, and asked them to submit a personal email address immediately—because access to their computer, email and files was about to be switched off.Severance is not cheap. Oracle booked $1.8 billion in restructuring costs in FY2026, up from $374 million a year earlier, a 391% jump. Its 10-K, filed on June 22, capped the total expected cost of the plan at $2.1 billion, which leaves only about $300 million of headroom. Cuts at the scale Business Insider describes would either have to fit inside that remainder or push Oracle into its second new restructuring plan in three years. TD Cowen analysts estimated in January that shedding 20,000 to 30,000 workers could unlock $8 billion to $10 billion.The money is going somewhere specific. Capital expenditure hit $55.7 billion in FY2026, up from $21.2 billion the year before, as Oracle raced to build data centres for customers including OpenAI. It raised $43 billion in debt and $5 billion in equity over the year, expects around $40 billion more in FY2027, and ran free cash flow of negative $23.7 billion. Interest expense alone climbed to $4.6 billion from $3.6 billion.The underlying business is not the problem. FY2026 revenue rose 17% to $67.4 billion, cloud infrastructure revenue grew 77%, and remaining performance obligations closed the year at $638 billion after ending Q3 at $553 billion. Oracle has also told investors that AI code generation is letting it reorganise product development into smaller teams, saying the technology helps it build "more software in less time with fewer people. "That sentence, written for shareholders in March, reads differently in August. Investors have not been won over either—the stock is down more than 20% this year, and shareholders sued in January over what Oracle said about how much it would need to borrow to service its $300 billion OpenAI commitment.For the employees on this month's lists, the reasoning is beside the point. The jobs are being removed to meet a date on a fiscal calendar, and the payoff Oracle is betting on will arrive after they have gone.
Article Summary: Oracle has burned through almost all of its $2.1 billion restructuring budget. Cuts would land on top of a year in which the company removed about 21,000 full- time roles. The company attributes part of the decline to the company's adoption and deployment of AI.
